basis: Purchase of an already listed company (decisions.md D5, T3): the firm's own archived text says BVP invested in James River Corp. in 1978 and 'James River was public at the time'; the company went public on 1973-03-16 (FundingUniverse company history, read 2026-10-06) and the firm lists no earlier private round. A later version of the firm's text dates the offering to 1980, which the company history does not support.

Financing of an already listed company (decisions.md D5, T3 / R3): AIT Group plc, later Portrait Software, was a London-listed company whose shares were suspended in 2002; the Evening Standard reports the rescue loan 'is to be provided by US-based Bessemer Venture Partners and a string of private investors' beside a rights issue and a move to AIM. The firm lists 2002 and no earlier private round.

BVP India purchase of an already listed company (decisions.md R3, T3): Tulip IT Services, later Tulip Telecom, listed on the BSE and NSE on 2006-01-05 after its December 2005 offering (chittorgarh.com IPO record, read 2026-10-06), and the firm's own list dates its investment to 2007 with no earlier private round.

note: Second pass: the firm's archived listing says Felda Hardymon and Don Feddersen 'led the company's first institutional round in 1987', read as Series A. The Y Combinator row named Parametric is a different company, a name collision.
Second pass: the firm's archived listing says Chris Gabrieli 'invested in the first institutional round' in 1987 and joined two more rounds, read as Series A.

Second pass: the firm's archived listing says Neill Brownstein 'invested in the first round' in 1979, read as Series A since nothing shows an earlier seed. Wikipedia: the maker of IBM-compatible mainframes declared bankruptcy in March 1983, so defunct. City from memory.

Second pass: the firm's own history page says Neill Brownstein 'led the turn-around financing of Tolerant Computing, later named Veritas Software'. A turn-around financing recapitalises a company that had already raised venture rounds, a later round, so Growth at medium confidence.

Second pass: the firm's archived listing of the same company under its older name (base row dick-s-clothing-sporting-goods) says 'BVP invested in the company's first institutional round'; the 2002 S-1 shows lettered preferred series A to G, so the first is read as Series A. The retailer dates from 1948, so this was growth capital in substance.

note: Second pass: the firm's archived listing says Chris Gabrieli 'led the first round in VistaCare', read as Series A since nothing shows an earlier seed. The 2002 S-1 confirms the Scottsdale headquarters.
Second pass: the firm's archived listing says David Cowan 'led the first venture round of Data Labs' in 1996, read as Series A; Yurie Systems bought it in December 1997.

Second pass: the firm's archived listing says 'In 1997 BVP led the first venture round of Webspective', read as Series A. Inktomi bought it in November 1999 for $106M in stock (Wikipedia, Inktomi). City (Andover, Massachusetts) from memory.

Second pass: the firm's own history page says Bruce Schneier 'turned to David Cowan at Bessemer to lead the Series A round in his startup Counterpane'.

Second pass: the firm's archived listing says 'BVP invested in both of the company's financing rounds in 2000', so it was in the first round (the firm's date 2000-01-11), read as Series A since nothing shows an earlier seed. City (Reston, Virginia) from memory.

Second pass: the firm's archived listing says David Cowan 'participated in all of Trigo's institutional rounds from its founding in 1999', so the entry is the first institutional round, read as Series A. City (Brisbane, California) from memory.

Second pass: the firm's archived listing says David Cowan 'led a round to fund ON's acquisition of DaVinci Systems' in 1994; ON Technology was founded in 1987 and venture-backed from the start, so this was a later round, Growth, from knowledge at medium confidence. Wikipedia dates the Symantec acquisition to October 2003 and the IPO to 1995.

note: Second pass: the December 1999 S-1 lists the preferred the Bessemer funds bought, starting with 344,187 shares of Series B on 1996-09-18 beside Charles River, then Series C, D and F. The record names the entry Series B, so Growth, although it was the first venture round after a small Series A. The S-1 confirms Cambridge.

Second pass: the 1999 S-1 lists a small Series A (about $1.5M over 1997 and April 1998), a $51.6M Series B in May 1998 and a Series C in April 1999, and the Bessemer funds signed the 1999 stockholders agreement. The firm's own year is 1998, which matches the Series B, so Growth at medium confidence. Interoute bought its European operations in 2005 (Wikipedia, Interoute) and the company deregistered in November 2005, so acquired with that successor.

Second pass: the March 2000 S-1 of Metapath Software International says Felda Hardymon sat on Metapath's board 'from its inception in December 1994', names the unit Metapath Software International (Bellevue) and shows Bessemer buying Class E and F preferred in 1997 and 1998. The firm says it joined every round from 1994 but no source names the first one (seed or Series A), so the stage stays undetermined.

Second pass: the firm's archived text calls it a 'manufacturer of microfiche systems' acquired by NCR in 1978, and says BVP invested in 1974 where its list says 1970; the list year is kept. City (Mountain View) from memory. No round named.

Second pass: EDGAR carries the company as NetOptix Corp, formerly Galileo Corp and Galileo Electro-Optics Corp of Sturbridge; Corning filed the merger communication on 2000-04-26 and the company deregistered on 2000-05-12, so acquired by Corning, 2000.

Second pass: EDGAR places Circadian Inc (electromedical apparatus) at 3942 North First Street, San Jose, and shows the SEC revoking its registration on 2011-04-25 with no filings on record, so it is read as defunct; what became of the business is not on record.

Second pass: the firm's archived listing says GMIS went public in 1991 and 'was later acquired by McKesson'; from knowledge the buyer was HBO & Company in 1997, which McKesson absorbed in 1999. EDGAR places GMIS Inc in Malvern, Pennsylvania.

Second pass: Wikipedia has PSINet filing for Chapter 11 on 2001-06-01 and Cogent Communications buying most of its United States assets in April 2002, so acquired with that successor rather than defunct (asset sale out of insolvency); last headquarters Ashburn, Virginia. Wikipedia names Matrix, Sigma and Amerindo as its venture investors, not the round Bessemer joined in 1993.

Second pass: West Corporation's 8-K/A says it completed on 2003-05-09 the purchase of InterCall by merging a subsidiary into its parent ITC Holding Company, Inc.; Magnolia Holding Company of Valley, Alabama then appears on EDGAR holding the group's ITC DeltaCom shares. An operating telecom group, acquired by West Corporation, 2003. City (West Point, Georgia) from memory.
